title: Implement pkg/testutils differential testing harness
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml (full PRD for pkg/testutils -- defines DiffTest struct, RunDiffTests API, normalization hooks, file-state comparison, and acceptance criteria)
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (pkg/testutils component description and its role as the acceptance gate for the pipeline)
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel01.0.yaml (test suite for ts -- shows how TimestampNormalizer and RunDiffTests are consumed by cmd/ts tests; confirms the API shape the harness must expose)
  - go.mod (module path and Go version)

files:
  - path: pkg/testutils/testutils.go
    action: create
    note: "DiffTest struct, Normalize function type, RunDiffTests entry point, binary execution, comparison and reporting, file-state comparison"
  - path: pkg/testutils/normalizers.go
    action: create
    note: "TimestampNormalizer and ComposeNormalizers helper"
  - path: pkg/testutils/testutils_test.go
    action: create
    note: "Unit tests for RunDiffTests, normalization composition, TimestampNormalizer, and file-state comparison"

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: |
      Define a DiffTest struct in pkg/testutils/testutils.go with these fields:
        - Name string (used as the t.Run subtest name)
        - Args []string (command-line arguments passed to both binaries)
        - Stdin []byte (stdin content; nil means no stdin / immediate EOF)
        - Env []string (environment variable overrides; nil means inherit test process env)
        - ExitCode int (expected exit code; compared against both binaries)
        - Normalize []func([]byte) []byte (slice of normalization functions applied in order before comparison; nil or empty means no normalization)
        - WorkDir string (optional working directory for both binaries; empty means use a per-test temp dir created by the harness)
        - ExpectedFiles map[string][]byte (optional; maps relative file paths to expected content after execution, for utilities like sponge whose output is a file rather than stdout)
  - id: R2
    text: |
      Implement a RunDiffTests function with signature:
        func RunDiffTests(t *testing.T, goBinary string, refBinary string, tests []DiffTest)
      For each DiffTest in the slice, call t.Run(test.Name, ...) to create a named subtest. Inside
      the subtest, execute both goBinary and refBinary with identical Args, Stdin, Env, and WorkDir.
      Use os/exec.Command. Set cmd.Stdin from test.Stdin (use bytes.NewReader; if nil, set to nil
      for immediate EOF). Set cmd.Env by merging os.Environ() with test.Env overrides (later entries
      override earlier ones for the same key). Capture stdout and stderr into bytes.Buffer. Capture
      the exit code from the *exec.ExitError or 0 on success.
  - id: R3
    text: |
      Impose a configurable timeout on each binary invocation. Use context.WithTimeout with a
      default of 10 seconds. Accept an optional Timeout time.Duration field on DiffTest (zero
      means use default). If either binary exceeds the timeout, fail the subtest with a message
      that includes which binary timed out, the args, and the timeout duration.
  - id: R4
    text: |
      After both binaries complete, apply the normalization chain. If test.Normalize is non-nil
      and non-empty, apply each function in order to both binaries' stdout and stderr bytes.
      The functions are applied sequentially: output of function N is input to function N+1.
  - id: R5
    text: |
      Compare normalized stdout byte-for-byte. Compare normalized stderr byte-for-byte. Compare
      exit codes exactly. If any differ, call t.Errorf with a failure message that includes:
      the DiffTest.Args, the Stdin content (truncated to 256 bytes if longer with a note
      "(truncated)"), the reference binary stdout, the Go binary stdout, the reference stderr,
      the Go stderr, both exit codes. A passing test must produce no output.
  - id: R6
    text: |
      When test.ExpectedFiles is non-nil, after both binaries complete, for each entry in
      ExpectedFiles read the file at the relative path (relative to the binary's WorkDir) and
      compare its content byte-for-byte to the expected []byte value. Report divergence in the
      same format as stdout divergence (showing expected vs actual file content).
  - id: R7
    text: |
      When test.WorkDir is empty, create a temporary directory via t.TempDir() for each binary
      invocation. The Go binary and reference binary each get their own temp dir to avoid
      interference. For file-state comparison (ExpectedFiles), run both binaries in separate
      copies of the same initial directory state -- copy the initial WorkDir contents to both
      temp dirs before execution, then compare the expected files in each temp dir.
  - id: R8
    text: |
      Implement TimestampNormalizer in pkg/testutils/normalizers.go as a func([]byte) []byte
      that replaces common timestamp patterns with the fixed string "TIMESTAMP". Patterns to
      match (using regexp):
        - Syslog format: "Jan  5 14:30:00" or "Feb 19 12:34:56" -- abbreviated month, space-padded day, HH:MM:SS
        - ISO-8601: "2024-01-05T14:30:00" with optional fractional seconds and Z or timezone offset
        - HH:MM:SS standalone (for -s and -i elapsed mode output)
        - Epoch with microseconds: digits.digits pattern like "1708358732.001234"
      The normalizer must handle multiple timestamps on the same line and across multiple lines.
  - id: R9
    text: |
      Implement a ComposeNormalizers function with signature:
        func ComposeNormalizers(fns ...func([]byte) []byte) func([]byte) []byte
      that returns a single normalizer applying all functions in order. This is a convenience
      for building the Normalize slice from individual normalizers.

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: |
      Package name is "testutils" under module path github.com/petar-djukic/go-unix-utils/pkg/testutils.
      The package is imported by cmd/<utility>/ test files. It must not import any cmd/ package.
  - id: D2
    text: |
      Use os/exec for binary execution. Do not shell out via bash or sh. Pass args directly
      to exec.Command(binary, args...). This avoids shell quoting issues and matches how
      Go test binaries are invoked.
  - id: D3
    text: |
      For environment merging, iterate os.Environ() first, then append test.Env entries.
      If test.Env contains a key already in os.Environ(), the test.Env value wins because
      exec.Cmd.Env uses the last occurrence of a key.
  - id: D4
    text: |
      The only external dependency allowed is golang.org/x/sys (already in go.mod per the
      architecture). pkg/testutils itself should need only the Go standard library.
  - id: D5
    text: |
      For the test file (testutils_test.go), write tests that use a simple test binary.
      Create a small Go program in testdata/ (e.g., testdata/echo/main.go) that echoes
      stdin to stdout with optional prefix, so RunDiffTests can be tested without requiring
      any Homebrew reference binary. Build it with "go build" in TestMain or use "go run"
      with the testdata path. This makes the tests self-contained and runnable in CI without
      brew dependencies.

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: |
      pkg/testutils compiles with "go build ./pkg/testutils/..." and produces no errors.
  - id: AC2
    text: |
      RunDiffTests runs each DiffTest as a named subtest visible in "go test -v" output.
  - id: AC3
    text: |
      A test case where both binaries produce identical output passes silently (no t.Errorf).
  - id: AC4
    text: |
      A test case where stdout differs between binaries fails with a message showing args,
      stdin, both stdouts, both stderrs, and both exit codes.
  - id: AC5
    text: |
      A test case that exceeds the timeout fails with a clear timeout message rather than
      hanging the test run.
  - id: AC6
    text: |
      TimestampNormalizer replaces syslog-format timestamps ("Feb 19 12:34:56") with
      "TIMESTAMP" and replaces HH:MM:SS patterns with "TIMESTAMP".
  - id: AC7
    text: |
      ComposeNormalizers applies normalizers in order -- output of first is input to second.
  - id: AC8
    text: |
      File-state comparison (ExpectedFiles) correctly detects when a binary writes different
      file content than expected.
  - id: AC9
    text: |
      "go test ./pkg/testutils/..." passes with all tests green.
  - id: AC10
    text: |
      golangci-lint run ./pkg/testutils/... produces no warnings. If golangci-lint is not
      installed or not configured, skip this check but ensure "go vet ./pkg/testutils/..."
      produces no warnings.
